title: FiniteSplitHypercoverExistence
statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$, a finite split étale hypercover of $X$ exists, as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover].

proof.text: Fix the full subsite of quasi-compact quasi-separated etale $X$-schemes. It contains $X$ and is closed under the finite limits used to form matching objects: fibre products are etale over $X$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and their quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness follow by applying [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to the projections and composites; equalizers are pullbacks of diagonals of quasi-separated etale objects. Hence when the terms through degree $n-1$ are finite unions of such objects, every component $T$ of $M_n(U)$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Cover $T$ by finitely many affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Restrict any etale covering of $T$ to each of those opens using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], then refine each restricted cover by finitely many affine opens of its members using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement]. Taking the union over the finite affine cover of $T$ gives a finite affine etale refinement of the original covering. Each chosen affine member is etale and of finite presentation over $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1).

proof.text: Construct a split hypercover by induction on $n$. In degree zero take a finite affine etale covering of $X$ from step 1. Given the split skeleton below $n$, form its matching object $M_n(U)$. The degeneracies already prescribe one copy of each earlier nondegenerate summand for every surjection $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$, $m<n$, and give maps from those copies to $M_n(U)$. On every matching component, including components met by degenerate copies, choose a finite affine etale covering as in step 1 and call the disjoint union of these new pieces $N_n$. Then $U_n$ is the coproduct of the degenerate copies with $N_n$; its map to $M_n(U)$ is a cover because $N_n$ covers every component. For a nondegenerate $n$-simplex, every proper face is the corresponding projection of its matching map, and those faces satisfy all face-face identities because they form a compatible point of $M_n(U)$. For a degenerate copy indexed by a surjection $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$ and an $m$-simplex $i$, compose any simplicial operator into $[n]$ with $\sigma$, factor that composite uniquely as a surjection followed by an injection, apply the old face indexed by the injection to $i$, and place the result in the degeneracy copy indexed by the surjection. This also defines each degeneracy of an old simplex as the corresponding copy. For two composable simplicial operators, the epi-mono factorization of their composite is the factorization obtained by repeating this rule, so their actions agree; when the last simplex is nondegenerate, the only extra case is two proper faces, already checked by the matching equations. This verifies the simplicial identities that Stacks 0DAV leaves implicit. Repeating for every $n$ gives a hypercover finite in each degree as defined in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover].
